static_findings.snippet: **This is a sub-skill of `css-development`** - typically invoked automatically via the main skill.
This skill validates against patterns documented in the main `css-development` skill:
**Action:** Check that Tailwind utilities are composed via `@apply`, not scattered in markup
- Are utilities composed into semantic classes via `@apply`?
**Action:** Verify colored and interactive elements have `dark:` variants
- Suggestion: Rename to `.button-secondary` for consistency with `.button-primary`
- Suggestion: Extract size to utility or rename to `.card-compact` for semantic meaning
1. **High priority:** Add dark mode variants to `.card-header` and `.badge` (visual bugs)
<!-- Utilities in markup instead of semantic class -->
- Similar patterns that could share a base class

content.user_title: Validate CSS Quality Against Project Patterns
content.value_statement: CSS reviews can miss naming, dark mode, composition, and test gaps. This skill guides a systematic validation pass with structured findings and fixes.
actual_capabilities: Reviews CSS class names for semantic and descriptive naming patterns.
Checks whether Tailwind utilities are composed through reusable CSS classes.
Identifies missing dark mode variants for colors and interactive states.
Finds repeated style patterns that could be extracted into shared classes.
Checks for static CSS tests and component rendering test coverage.
Produces a structured CSS validation report with file and line references.
limitations: Requires access to the relevant CSS and component files in the project.
Works best for projects that use Tailwind CSS and semantic component classes.
Does not run visual regression tests unless the surrounding agent does so.
Does not replace product design review or accessibility testing.

use_cases.title: Review CSS before a pull request
use_cases.description: Check new component styles for naming, composition, dark mode support, tests, and documentation before review.

use_cases.title: Audit design system consistency
use_cases.description: Compare existing CSS against shared project patterns and identify classes that should be renamed or extracted.

use_cases.title: Verify style test coverage
use_cases.description: Find important semantic classes that lack static CSS checks or component rendering tests.

prompt_templates.title: Basic CSS Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this CSS file for semantic class names, Tailwind composition, dark mode coverage, tests, and documentation.

prompt_templates.title: Component Style Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Review styles and related components together.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the component styles in this feature. Include CSS files, component usage, and any tests that verify class usage.

prompt_templates.title: Design System Consistency Check
prompt_templates.scenario: Check multiple files against established project patterns.
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate these CSS changes against our design system patterns. Report naming issues, repeated utility groups, and missing dark mode variants.

prompt_templates.title: Pre-Merge CSS Quality Gate
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before merging a larger change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a full CSS validation pass for this branch. Prioritize user-visible risks, missing tests, and refactor opportunities with file and line references.

output_examples.input: A stylesheet with mixed semantic classes, repeated utilities, and partial dark mode support.
output: A validation report listing good patterns, naming issues, missing dark mode variants, and repeated style groups.
Prioritized recommendations with affected files, estimated impact, and suggested class names.

output_examples.input: A component change that adds new CSS classes without tests.
output: A review note identifying which classes lack static CSS tests and rendering tests.
Suggested test coverage areas described in plain language, without changing code automatically.

output_examples.input: A design system cleanup request for cards, buttons, badges, and empty states.
output: A structured audit that groups findings by semantic naming, composition, documentation, and visual mode coverage.
Recommended next actions sorted by user impact and implementation effort.

best_practices: Provide the main stylesheet, related component files, and existing tests in the same request.
Ask for file and line references so findings can be reviewed and fixed quickly.
Run the skill before broad refactors so naming and composition issues are visible first.
anti_patterns: Do not use it as a substitute for browser-based visual checks when layout risk is high.
Do not apply Tailwind-specific recommendations to projects that do not use Tailwind.
Do not request automatic fixes before reviewing the validation report and priorities.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews CSS naming, Tailwind composition, dark mode variants, repeated patterns, tests, and documentation.

faq.question: Does it edit CSS automatically?
faq.answer: No. It first produces a validation report and asks what should happen next.

faq.question: Is this only for Tailwind projects?
faq.answer: It is most useful for Tailwind projects, but semantic naming and documentation checks can help other CSS codebases.

faq.question: Can it find missing dark mode styles?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks colored and interactive styles for missing dark mode variants.

faq.question: Can it check test coverage?
faq.answer: Yes. It looks for static stylesheet tests and component rendering tests that verify class usage.
